newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Barak new head of Israel Labour party - exit polls.
newsitem.headline: Barak new head of Israel Labour party - exit polls.

text.p: Israel's main opposition Labour party elected former army chief Ehud Barak on Tuesday as its new leader, according to exit polls.
Israel Television's exit poll gave Barak 57 percent of the vote by party members compared with 28 percent for Yossi Beilin.
Channel Two's poll showed 56 percent support for Barak with 26 percent of the votes going to Beilin. Official results were expected early on Wednesday.
"If these will be the real results, this is truly a good showing for (candidate) number one but also a nice showing for number two," Beilin told reporters at Labour party headquarters.
The winner of the contest is expected to face Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in national elections scheduled for 2000.
Opinion polls have shown Barak neck-and-neck with Netanyahu, 47, whose first year in office has been buffeted by peacemaking crises and clouded by corruption allegations.
The leadership vote marked a milestone for Labour -- a passing of the political torch from former prime minister Peres, 73, and his slain predecessor Yitzhak Rabin.
Their rival camps ruled the often contentious party for nearly a quarter-century.
The heavily favoured Barak, 55, has cast himself as heir to Rabin's warrior-turned-peacemaker mantle.
